Start by observing the cascade: run `kubectl -n dojo-chaos-dep scale deploy/backend --replicas=0` and watch `kubectl -n dojo-chaos-dep get pods -w`. Within ~10 seconds the app pods go NotReady. Then inspect the probe that caused it: `kubectl -n dojo-chaos-dep get deploy app -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].readinessProbe}' && echo`. Scale backend back to 2 before attempting your fix.

The fix is in the readinessProbe type. Change it from `exec` (which runs `wget http://backend-svc/` inside the container) to `httpGet` pointing at the app's own port — for example `httpGet: {path: /, port: 80}`. Default nginx always returns 200 on `/`, so this probe answers 'is my process up?' rather than 'is my upstream up?'. Also add `resources.requests` (cpu + memory) to the app container.

For a production-grade fix: create a ConfigMap with an nginx `server {}` block that (1) serves `return 200 'ok'` on `/healthz` — use this as your readinessProbe path, (2) `proxy_pass`es `/` to `backend-svc:80` with `proxy_connect_timeout 2s`, and (3) uses `error_page 502 503 504 = @fallback` with a named location that returns a static degraded response. Mount the ConfigMap at `/etc/nginx/conf.d` and switch the readinessProbe to `httpGet: {path: /healthz, port: 80}`.
